newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end down, focus on mid-cap stocks.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end down, focus on mid-cap stocks.

text.p: Shares at Bombay exchanges closed with modest losses on Tuesday, as lack of buying support led to a sell-off in frontline stocks, traders said.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index lost 33.18 points, or 0.89 percent, to end at a provisional 3,702.07, off 3,742.40 -- the intra-day high.
Fund activity was mainly concentrated in select second-tier stocks due to cheaper valuations, they said.

"There is fund buying in many mid-cap stocks," said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers. "But, nobody wants to buy agressively due to the recent poor results announced by major firms," Sequeira added.
Foreign funds were buyers in stocks including TVS Suzuki, HDFC Bank, Carrier Aircorn, Cipla and Hero Honda, players said.
Analysts said India's leading two-wheeler maker Bajaj Auto will see sluggish growth in the financial year ended March 31, 1997, when a prolonged industrial slowdown hit vehicle sales.

They said the firm -- which is among the world's largest two wheeler-makers -- was likely to announce a net profit of 4.5 billion rupees ($125 million), up some eight percent from 4.18 billion in 1995/96. Earnings are due on Wednesday.

Bajaj Auto's net profit had surged nearly 40 percent in 1995/96, over the previous year."The sales slowdown is a reflection of the general weakness in the economy," said K.N. Sreenivasan, automobile analyst at Jardine Fleming India Broking.
Bajaj Auto shares ended 3.75 rupees up at 850.0.
Reliance Industries, Indo-Gulf Fertilisers, Crompton Greaves and Grasim recently announced a fall in 1997/98 net profits.
Most analysts feel that a cautious outlook for US stocks after an extended bull run could trigger some fund flow in India from those allocated to emerging markets.

A blistering 123 point rally at Wall Street helped the Dow Jones close at a record high of 7,292.75 on Monday. The Dow's jump came as Wall Street bet that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged at a policy-setting meeting next week.
